selection_rule: STEP 4: Tier 1 (A2) first. npm run measure:amirnet-coverage was run before selection (1108/3382 existing). The 253 Tier-1 headwords still missing from the bank were computed directly (data/amirnet-vocab.csv tier=1 minus every headword already present across data/generated/batch-*.jsonl). Of those 253, this batch took 20 straightforward, concrete A2 nouns/verbs/one pronoun that support clean, allowed-vocabulary example sentences without difficulty. The remaining ~233 (including all British/American spelling-variant CSV rows, which the coverage script matches by the CSV's exact slash-joined string and so will keep reading as "missing" no matter which single spelling is written) are left for a future tick, ideally once T-353's verify regression is fixed so word-only rows can close the gap at real volume.
gate_method: gateSense (lib/core/contentSchema.ts) run directly against every row with the production allowed-words set (data/generated/allowed-words-2026-08-07.txt), the same file scripts/measure-gate.mjs loads — not just measure:gate after the fact. First draft had 8 words fail on level drift (fountain/vase/mall on 'center'; kindness on 'society'; clever on 'solution'; icy on 'speed'; thief/candy/bicycle on 'steal'; fierce on 'structure'; bold on 'style'; risky on 'success') — every one substituted with a plain, common alternative and re-gated: 0/20 rejected on the second pass. npm run measure:gate (all 50 batch files now) confirmed 0 rejected afterward.
distractor_review_note: Every distractor was checked by hand against the near-synonym trap (lesson-file §A1 rule 2): dropped 'noise' for sound (too close a synonym), 'origin' for source, 'answer' for solution, 'power' for strength, 'rob' for steal, and 'victory' for success — all replaced with related-but-distinct words (e.g. silence/music for sound; river/cause for source; problem/method for solution; energy/weakness for strength; borrow/hide for steal; effort/failure for success) before finalizing.
translation_confidence_note: 20/20 rows are translation_confidence:"high" — every headword is a concrete, unambiguous A2 word, and its example pair pins the sense the translation carries (e.g. 'space' as room-to-move, not outer space).
batch_size_note: 20 rows, full apparatus, all Tier 1 (A2). Sized to what could be hand-authored, checked word-by-word against the production allowed-words set with the real gateSense function (not assumed), and pushed through the full verify gate. Well under the 1,200-row-per-file ceiling.
